why: The whole run but the stills, on the P1S's K5 profile seeded into the instance's own config: the base radii searched against CamProfile's pressure angle, every part verified and checked as it prints (check_print, in its print direction), the pegged panels, the bushings and the crank, the assembly with both followers on contact relations and both levers closed through links, the assembly sequence, the crank turn and the chop as mesh studies with every press relieved, check_followers over both, the requirements, the negative controls (the short dwell failing drop_rpm, the small base failing the pressure angle, two guides refused as contacts), the FEM of the camshaft, the crank and the handle's pin on pins with every load from check_followers and every study's statics to 1 %, and the print plate's every check_print item.
markers: every part checked as it prints \(25 parts, 44 pieces\): every item passes
assembly sequence: 30 steps, every one goes home
study turn: 49 samples, mesh at .*: clean
study chop: 41 samples, mesh at .*: clean
negative control, the axe's dwell at .*requirement fail
negative control, the bird's cam on base .*requirement fail
negative control, a guide tilted: refused
FEM: the camshaft holds its working load, and every study's pins answer its loads' force and moment within 1 %
plate 1: 44 pieces, every check_print item passes

readme.runs: `woodcutter/build.py --no-render` on the seeded P1S profile: the base radii searched against CamProfile's pressure angle, every part checked as it prints, the pegged box, bushings and crank, the mechanism with both contact followers and their lever loops, the assembly sequence, the crank turn and the chop (mesh, every press relieved), `check_followers` over both, every requirement, the negative controls (a short dwell, a small base, two guides off the cam), the FEM of the loaded parts on pins and their statics, and the print plate's `check_print`
